did.abstract: Mary Ellen Carroll (b. 1961) is a conceptual artist whose work examines architectural, systemic, and organizational practices across a wide range of media. Her work spans multiple disciplines including: architecture, writing, performance, photography, filmmaking, printmaking, sculpture, and painting. The Mary Ellen Carroll Papers (dated 1960–2017, 2026-present) consist of materials created and collected by Carroll over the course of her life and career. The collection includes publications; artists' books; exhibition catalogs and promotional materials; correspondence; photographs; administrative paperwork; teaching and conference materials; original artworks; archived websites; and ephemera accumulated throughout her personal and professional endeavors.
did.langmaterial: The majority of materials are in English, but there are also some materials in Spanish, German, and Korean.

bioghist.head: Biographical Note
bioghist.p: Mary Ellen Carroll (b. 1961) is a New York City based conceptual artist whose work examines architectural, systemic, and organizational practices across a wide range of media. Carroll was born in Illinois, received her Bachelor of Science degree from the University of Colorado at Boulder, and her Master in Fine Arts degree from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago.

One of Carroll's most significant ongoing projects, prototype-81, which was initiated in 1999, involves the physical rotation and transformation of a house in Houston, Texas, functioning as both a conceptual artwork and an intervention into urban development and policy. Her other notable works include Itinerant Gastronomy (1996), Me vs. I (2000), Mistakes and Lies, Part Two (2001), THE TONI NEGRI (Drinking From the Same Glass) (2001), 100 Artists See God (2003–2005), Federal (2005), indestructible language (2006), Weather Report: Art and Climate Change (2007), No Zoning: Artists Engage Houston (2009), The Baghdad Batteries (2010), Model Theories (2012), and the Circle Games (2016)

Carroll's work has been exhibited internationally at major institutions including the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York City; the Institute of Contemporary Arts (ICA) in London; MoMA PS1 in New York City; the Menil Collection in Houston; and venues in Vienna, Zurich, and Dubai.

Carroll has also published several books including A Modest Proposal/A Modist Prepozel (1994), Without Intent (1996), 100 German Men (1998), All the men that think they can be me (2004), and MEC (2010).

In addition to her artistic practice, Carroll is a lecturer and educator. She has contributed to programs in art, architecture, and public policy at institutions such as Columbia University, Yale University, Princeton University, the University of California Irvine, and Rice University.

Carroll is the recipient of numerous grants and honors including the Guna S. Mundheim Fellow in the Visual Arts at the American Academy in Berlin, a Graham Foundation Fellowship for prototype-81, and the AIA's Artist of the Year Award. She has received a Guggenheim Fellowship, two Pollock/Krasner Awards, a Rockefeller Foundation Fellowship, and a MacDowell Colony Fellowship.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This collection is arranged into two series and six subseries. Materials have been arranged in alphabetical order by topic within each series and subseries.
Subseries I.A: Artwork, Exhibitions, Architecture, and Film Projects
Subseries I.D: Teaching, Conferences, and Lectures

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Mary Ellen Carroll Papers (dated 1960–2017, 2026-ongoing) document both Carroll's conceptual art practice and aspects of her personal life. The collection includes publications featuring articles by Carroll and those about her; notebooks and sketchbooks; writings; correspondence; administrative paperwork; materials related to exhibitions and projects; artist's books; promotional items such as flyers, posters, press releases, and brochures related to exhibitions and projects; photographs; teaching materials, including lecture notes and syllabi; archived websites; and original artworks. Carroll's personal life is represented in photographs, correspondence, childhood mementos, books gifted to Carroll with personalized notes, awards, diplomas, and a scrapbook. Materials are available in paper, analog audiovisual, and digital formats.

This collection also includes Mary Ellen Carroll's archived website for her studio and her artwork, prototype-81. Her website contains descriptions and images of her writings, public presentations, and art; and news related to exhibitions and awards.

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: Materials housed in Boxes 38-48 are restricted until the donor's death. All other material is open without restriction.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Materials were transferred from Mary Ellen Carroll's studio in multiple installments in 2012, 2014, 2015, and 2017. The accession numbers associated with these gifts are 2012.347, 2014.347, 2015.347, 2016.001, 2018.113, and 2019.022.

In March 2026, https://mecarroll.com/ and https://prototype180.org/ were selected by curator Nicholas Martin and captured through the use of Archive-It. Archive-It uses web crawling technology to capture websites at a scheduled time and displays only an archived copy, from the resulting WARC file, of the website. The accession number associated with these websites is 2026.010.

phystech.head: Audiovisual Access Policies and Procedures
phystech.p: Audiovisual materials have not been preserved and may not be available to researchers. Materials not yet digitized will need to have access copies made before they can be used. To request an access copy, or if you are unsure if an item has been digitized, please contact NYU Special Collections (special.collections@nyu.edu, 212-998-2596) with the collection name, collection number, and a description of the item(s) requested. A staff member will respond to you with further information.

phystech.head: Born-Digital Access Policies and Procedures
phystech.p: An access terminal for born-digital materials in the collection is available by appointment for reading room viewing and listening only. Researchers may view an item's original container and/or carrier, but the physical carriers themselves are not available for use because of preservation concerns.

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: Identification of item, date; Mary Ellen Carroll Papers; MSS 347; box number; folder number or item identifier; Fales Library and Special Collections, New York University.
To cite the archived websites in this collection: Identification of item, date; Mary Ellen Carroll Papers; MSS 347; Wayback URL; Fales Library and Special Collections, New York University.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: At the time of accessioning, materials were moved into archival housing and a collection-level finding aid was created to describe these materials. No physical processing or arrangement was performed at this time. Born-digital objects were identified and inventoried, but were not forensically imaged, analyzed, or described at this time.
In September 2017, three sculptures, one photograph and photostat installation, four blankets, and five artworks were prepared to be moved to offsite art storage in September 2017.
In March 2019, material was placed in an acid-free folder and box, and oversized material was rolled and placed in a poster storage box.
Box 23 was created in error and was deleted in February 2021.

In August 2025, six artworks were deaccessioned from the collection and returned to Mary Ellen Carroll at her request. In September 2025, one additional artwork was deaccessioned and returned to Carroll at her request.

The collection was processed and described by an archivist in spring 2026. Materials were rehoused into archival folders and boxes. Original titles, if applicable, were retained, but in some instances, new titles were assigned to better reflect the folder's contents. Materials were arranged into series and subseries by topic and then organized alphabetically by file title. Related materials were grouped together intellectually and physically, when possible. Photographs, negatives, and slides were removed from their original housing and placed into archival sleeves. Duplicate materials and materials that did not fit within the scope of the collection were removed and returned to the donor.
18 audiovisual items were assigned a media ID and housed appropriately.

New York University Libraries follow professional standards and best practices when imaging, ingesting, and processing born-digital material in order to maintain the integrity and authenticity of the content. 18 optical discs, 3 floppy disks, and 45 zip disks were forensically imaged and analyzed using Exact Audio Copy, Isobuster, and Forensic Toolkit. The electronic records were intellectually incorporated into the finding aid.

One scrapbook was stabilized and rehoused by conservators from New York University's Barbara Goldsmith Preservation and Conservation Department. Conservators also rehoused realia related to Itinerant Gastronomy; rehoused and stabilized four artpieces from the Robinson Crusoe project; flattened a selection of posters related to Carroll's works; and placed oversized posters into rolled storage.
In April 2026, Subseries I.F. was added and additional descriptive information related to the archived websites were added to the finding aid.

In September 2026, five boxes containing restricted materials were rehoused into archival folders and archival boxes. These materials were intellectually incorporated into their appropriate series within the inventory and access restrictions were noted at the file level for each item(s). At this time, medical records and tax returns were removed the from collection.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: This collection is protected by copyright and/or related rights. You are free to use materials in the collection in any way that is permitted by the copyright and related rights legislation that applies to your use. For other uses you need to obtain permission from the rights-holder(s).

appraisal.head: Appraisal
appraisal.p: In August 2025, the following artworks that were originally part of the collection were deaccessioned and returned to Mary Ellen Carroll at her request: Item MSS.347.cuid6206 Metric Time [Digital sign] Boxes 30-32 and cuid6021a-d The Hand of Fatima/Keep Me Modest (cuid6023; cuid6021a-d) Item MSS.347.cuid6024 and 34 Eames 2 to 1 Item MSS.347.cuid6025 Free Throw Item 33 Indestructible Language Item MSS.347.cuid6022 The Toni Negri (Drinking From The Same Glass)
In September 2025, the following artwork was also deaccessioned and returned to Carroll: Item 2012.18 Feigned Respect

During the course of processing in 2026, the following materials were removed the the collection: duplicate materials; two blanks copies of The Science of Genocide; reports related to the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation and Guggenheim fellow candidate applications; commercially available travel guidebooks and maps; theater and concert playbills from performances Carroll attended; financial documents with personal identifiable information and account numbers; health records; employee files and resumes; papers related to Carroll's home renovation; computer software discs; campaign ephemera related to President Barack Obama; rolled uncut galley proofs of MEC; and off air recordings and commercially available films.

Publications including, but not limited to, the New York Times Magazine, Food & Wine Magazine, The New Yorker, Artforum, Gourmet, Time Out, Die Presse (German newspaper), The New York Times, Back Stage, The New York Sun, The Boston Globe, The Village Voice, and The Houston Chronicle were removed from the collection once articles related to Carroll were photocopied.

The following types of photographs were removed from the collection: duplicates; out of focus and blurry images; portraits and candids of individual friends and groups, with the exception of those including Mary Ellen Carroll; intimate personal family photos; and unidentified or generic objects and locations.
In September 2026, medical records and tax returns were removed from the collection.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series focuses on Mary Ellen Carroll's career as a working artist, author, and teacher. This series documents Carroll's artistic works, architectural projects, exhibitions, film projects, writing, and teaching through administrative documents, architectural drawings, correspondence, ephemera, handwritten notes, photographs, press coverage, archived websites, and writings in various stages of completion.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries includes a wide range of materials that document Carroll's exhibitions, art projects, architectural projects, and film projects. Major projects prominently documented in this subseries include Itinerant Gastronomy, Federal, prototype-180, the TONI NEGRI (Drinking from the Same Glass), Canco Lofts, Me v. I, OFPC '99, the Circle Game, and Mistakes and Lies, Part Two.

This subseries includes promotional materials for numerous exhibitions in the form of postcards, programs, flyers, and circulars. Documentation of Itinerant Gastronomy includes posters, feast menus, customized realia, press clippings, print and digital photographs, and recordings of her experimental culinary project. Materials for Federal include promotional materials, clippings, posters, emails, and VHS copies of her film. The Circle Game is represented through photographs and press clippings, while the TONI NEGRI (Drinking from the Same Glass) fountain is documented with photographs, correspondence, press clippings, and architectural drawings. Materials related to prototype-180 include photographs and papers. Carroll's Canco Lofts architectural project is documented by correspondence, promotional materials, administrative records, architectural drawings, and digital renderings -- all of which are present in both paper and digital formats. Materials related to Me v. I and Mistakes and Lies, Part Two consist of video recordings and supporting documentation detailing their production.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries comprises artistically modified copies of Daniel DeFoe's novel Robinson Crusoe. Carroll distributed multiple copies of the book to various artists, asked them to alter the text or pages creatively, and return the works to her as art pieces. Some of the art pieces feature photographs and drawings; others incorporate objects such as a bar of soap or an encased beetle; and additional versions include other unique interventions such as painting the book to look like a VHS tape or replacing the novel's content with another book.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This subseries is arranged in alphabetical order by the participating artist's last name, with the exception of the list documenting particiating artists, which has been placed at the top of the subseries inventory.

bioghist.head: Historical Note
bioghist.p: In 1992, on behalf of Emilio Fantin, an Italian artist working in Bologna, Mary Ellen Carroll distributed multiple copies of Daniel DeFoe's novel, Robinson Crusoe, to various artists. According to a circular Carroll included with the books, "This book is one of fifty copies of Robinson Crusoe that have been distributed in New York. It will be part of a piece by Emilio Fantin, an Italian artist working in Bologna. His piece consists of a suitcase filled with catalogs on Italian artists, an address book with my name and telephone number, and a roundrip plane ticket to New York for the individual who purchases the piece. I will fill the suitcase with materials that you send me, as well as creating another suitcase that will be filled with the copies of Robinson Crusoe. You may do with the book as you please. I ask that you sign the inside cover beneath your name and return it to me within one month with the enclosed postage."

physdesc.extent: in 10 manuscript boxes and 1 flat file folder

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries focuses on Mary Ellen Carroll's written works, press about her, and interviews. Copies of articles and excerpts from books written by Carroll, as well as copies of articles about Carroll and those that mention her are also included in this subseries. In addition to these published materials, the subseries features notebooks with Carroll's handwritten notes and ideas, along with sketches and conceptual drawings. Essays written by others, which include Carroll's handwritten edits and margin notes, and interviews with Carroll are also found in this subseries.

This subseries contains drafts, proofs, correspondence, press, and publications related to Carroll's monograph MEC (2010), published by Steidl/MACK. This subseries also contains copies and documents related to Carroll's other written works including A Modest Proposal/A Modist Prepozel (1994), Without Intent (1996), and All the men who think they can be me (2004). Materials documenting to Carroll's photography project 100 German Men (1998) include copies of the publication, correspondence, press releases, reviews, and digital photographs of the men featured in the project.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries contains teaching materials related to architecture and public policy courses from Carroll's appointments at Rice University in Houston, Texas and the University of California Irvine. Carroll also spent time at the Pusan National University in Busan, South Korea, and while her teaching materials are not included in the collection, her involvement in the Busan Bienniale is documented through programs, presentation notes, promotional materials, architectural blueprints, a signed visitor's book, and brochures. This subseries also includes conference and lecture materials.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries documents the logistical and administrative aspects of Mary Ellen Carroll's career. It includes address books and personal agendas; correspondence; art loan agreements and contracts; grant applications; artist residency records; travel paperwork and itineraries; art installation instructions; Carroll's business cards and curriculum vitae; inventories; and materials pertaining to her company, MEC studios, incorporated. Both physical and digital documents related to the Robert Blanchon Estate Project and Robert Blanchon are also found in this subseries. Carroll and Blanchon were close friends and collaborators, and she served as the representative of his estate following his death in 1999.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries contains Mary Ellen Carroll's archived website for her studio and her artwork, prototype-81. Her website contains descriptions and images of her writings, public presentations, and art. The website also includes news related to exhibitions and awards.

phystech.head: Physical Characteristics and Technical Requirements
phystech.p: Due to technical or privacy issues, archived websites may not be exact copies of the original website at the time of the web crawl. Certain file types will not be captured dependent on how they are embedded in the site. Other parts of websites that the crawler has difficulty capturing includes Javascript, streaming content, database-driven content, and highly interactive content. Full-Text searches of archived websites are available at https://archive-it.org/organizations/567.
